transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 mins
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Northvale Head of ML), Priya Nair (Northvale Platform Eng), Marco Diaz (Northvale Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick renewal/expansion sync, discuss EU private node onboarding, capacity bump x2, procurement timeline, technical check for latency regression testing.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, quick agenda — renewal & capacity, EU private onboarding, and then technical follow-ups. Is that right on your side, Ethan?
[00:12] Ethan: Yeah that's right, Samira. We're getting close to the end of Q1 budget cycle and want to lock down the capacity numbers. We're seeing about a 70% uptick month-on-month in the chat assistant workload.
[00:22] Priya: And the EU residency bit is non-negotiable for a couple of clients. We prefer private nodes in eu-west, ideally customer-managed networking.
[00:31] Samira: Got it. High level: you can do a hybrid — keep the hosted baseline, reserve Dedicated for steady throughput, and add Private (VPC) in eu-west for residency. Liam I'll hand to you for the technical tradeoffs.
[00:42] Liam: Sure. The main differences to call out — Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation; Private gives you VPC + KMS control and audit logs in-region. There's a small delta in per-token cost due to node sizing and egress. For latency: Private in-region will cut roundtrip by 30-60ms compared to a distant hosted region, but we need to account for cold starts and batch sizing.
[01:10] Ethan: Can you quantify that delta? Our 90th percentile target is 250ms for short text completions (<=256 tokens). Right now some spikes hit 420ms.
[01:20] Liam: With local private nodes and optimized batching/prefix caching we usually shave those spikes enough to be within 250-300ms 90th, depending on model choice and KV cache hit-rate. If you pin a lighter quantized variant we can help too. There's a tradeoff: more quantization lowers cost but can affect subtle output quality.
[01:45] Priya: What about failover? If eu-west is unavailable, do requests route to hosted? Any auto-fallback?
[01:52] Liam: Yes, smart routing can fail over to a nearby region or a lower-cost variant. We recommend canary routing first, then automatic fallback configured in the route policy. We'll share a playbook.
[02:05] Marco: From procurement, timelines — we need a PO by end of March. But approvals might slip; can you provide a quote with line items for dedicated baseline, burst, and eu private add-on? Also need an explanation of data residency compliance.
[02:20] Samira: Absolutely. We'll put together a tiered quote: baseline (current commit), + 2x capacity uplift option, and EU private node cost. We'll include the SLA and SOC2/ISO references.
[02:30] Ethan: For the benchmarks you mentioned, what does Redwood need from us?
[02:35] Liam: Ideally: 1) current QPS and peak-hour traffic profile, 2) typical prompt length and token distribution, 3) any heavy multi-turn chat patterns that keep long KV caches. With that we can recommend batching window, KV cache TTL, and quantization profile.
[02:52] Ethan: We can pull the QPS + 90/95/99 latency histograms. Priya will attach the traffic profile.
[03:00] Priya: Yup, I'll export the last 30 days and share.
[03:05] Marco: Also, on KMS — we use CloudKey at the moment. Any compatibility issues?
[03:12] Liam: We integrate with customer KMS via standard KMS APIs; some HSM-backed flows require a short security review but generally straightforward. We'll put together the KMS integration doc.
[03:25] Samira: Noted. Security docs will be in the package. We'll link SOC2 report, SSO/SAML guide, and the KMS integration checklist.
[03:35] Ethan: A few nitty-gritty items — token billing: does EU private change token accounting? We need per-route cost breakdowns for our finance team.
[03:45] Samira: The billing is per-token but we can break down by model/route and include region-specific surcharges. The console shows token-level cost, and we'll include a sample export for you.
[04:00] Priya: On the technical side, can we run a short benchmark before committing? Like a 24-hour soak with a mirrored traffic replay?
[04:07] Liam: Yes, we can run a benchmark plan. Two options: 1) small pilot on private nodes with a limited window, or 2) a replay bench where you push a copy of traffic to a test cluster. Option 2 mirrors production more closely but requires a replay infra on your side.
[04:25] Ethan: Replay might be heavy. Could we do a hybrid: baseline replay for peak hours + production shadowing?
[04:32] Liam: That's reasonable. We'll document the steps and provide a runbook. It'll include method to mask PII if needed and expected metrics to collect (p95, p99, KV hit-rate, token throughput, GPU utilization).
[04:50] Marco: Timeline constraints: PO by end of March, procurement prefers 60-day payment terms, and we need a legal appendix for data residency. Who will own the contract updates?
[05:00] Samira: I'll coordinate with Legal. We'll prepare a redline-ready amendment for EU private nodes and include the appendix language for data residency and KMS. Marco, can you confirm the procurement contact and their contract review SLA?
[05:12] Marco: I'll send that over after this call.
[05:15] Samira: Great. A couple of customer concerns we've seen elsewhere — quality regressions when moving to quantized models. We'll propose a canary rollout: holdout prompt set that you already have, run evaluation pre/post, and a rollback policy.
[05:30] Ethan: We do have an eval set for our assistant; will share that. We also want to track hallucination metrics across rollouts.
[05:40] Liam: We'll include quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to your prompt set — Redwood Optimize can surface deltas by prompt.
[05:50] Priya: Any surprises on network egress costs? If we keep data flow internal to eu-west private nodes, egress should be minimal but cross-region failover might incur egress if routed to another region.
[06:05] Samira: Correct — we'll call out egress scenarios in the quote and show cost delta for cross-region fallback.
[06:12] Ethan: Ok, happy with that. Can you also include an estimate for peak-day burst capacity? We sometimes have trading-day-like surges.
[06:20] Liam: We'll add a burst buffer option with pricing per peak-GPU-hour. Also suggestions on queueing and backpressure to keep tail-latencies controlled.
[06:35] Marco: On the procurement doc, we need the invoice remit address and tax ID up front.
[06:40] Samira: We'll include all that.
[06:45] Ethan: Anything else on security? We might request a short SOC2 addendum describing data residency controls.
[06:52] Samira: We'll attach the SOC2 report and addendum language. If you need an onsite audit or more detailed logs, we can discuss enterprise package add-ons.
[07:05] Priya: Last question: how long to spin up the EU private nodes once PO is signed?
[07:12] Liam: Typical time is 3-6 weeks depending on capacity and networking signoff. If you want faster, there's a fast-track option with a one-time setup fee — we'll include timelines on the quote.
[07:25] Ethan: Good. Let's summarize next steps.
[07:28] Samira: Action items — we'll share the formal quote with line items (by 02/24), include the KMS and SOC2 docs, and Liam will publish the benchmark runbook. Ethan/Priya will send traffic & eval sets. Marco will confirm procurement timelines and contact. Schedule a 2-hour technical deep-dive next week — Samira will propose slots.
[07:50] Marco: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:52] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the links to the benchmark deck and the PRICING attachment.
[07:58] End of call.

References mentioned:
